instruction.text: Is the statement true or false?

atoms.a: There are no seven-digit numbers greater than <mat>9999999</mat>.
There are no six-digit numbers smaller than <mat>111100</mat>.

correct.text: That’s right. The smallest six-digit number is actually <mat>100000</mat>.

atoms.a: Every seven-digit number has a seven-digit number that comes after it.

correct.text: That’s right. The number that comes after <mat>9999999</mat> is the eight-digit number <mat>10000000</mat>.

atoms.a: The smallest five-digit number that has only one 0 is <mat>11110</mat>.

correct.text: That’s right. The smallest five-digit number that has only one 0 is actually <mat>10111</mat>.

atoms.a: The largest five-digit number without a 9 is <mat>88888</mat>.
One billion is different from one million because it has one extra zero.

correct.text: That’s right. One million has six zeros and one billion has nine zeros. Therefore, the difference is actually 3 extra zeros.
